subject: Vocabulary
description: Words for character — meticulous, gregarious, magnanimous, frugal, garrulous, taciturn

questions.stem: A MAGNANIMOUS person is one who is:

options.option_text: Stingy and unwilling to share
Generous and forgiving in spirit
Loud and aggressive in nature
Sad and easily depressed often

questions.explanation: MAGNANIMOUS — Latin 'magnus' (great) + 'animus' (spirit). Generous, especially toward defeated rivals; willing to forgive; noble in spirit. 'In victory he was magnanimous.' Distractor 1 = miserly, parsimonious. Distractor 3 = boisterous. Distractor 4 = melancholic.
questions.subject: Vocabulary

options.option_text: Prefers complete solitude always
Enjoys company of others, sociable
Acts hostile to all newcomers
Stays silent in any situation

questions.explanation: GREGARIOUS — sociable, fond of company. From Latin 'grex' (flock, herd) — like animals that live in groups. 'A gregarious extrovert.' Distractor 1 = solitary / introverted. Distractor 3 = misanthropic. Distractor 4 = taciturn.
questions.subject: Vocabulary

questions.stem: A METICULOUS worker is one who is:

options.option_text: Casual and quick in work habits
Extremely careful about every detail
Slow and lazy in completing tasks
Loud about all of their accomplishments

questions.explanation: METICULOUS — paying great attention to detail; very careful. 'A meticulous accountant catches every error.' From Latin 'meticulosus' (fearful — original sense). Distractor 1 = careless, slipshod. Distractor 3 = lethargic. Distractor 4 = boastful.
questions.subject: Vocabulary

options.option_text: Spend money lavishly without care
Be careful with money and avoid waste
Borrow heavily and spend recklessly
Refuse to talk about any finances

questions.explanation: FRUGAL — economical, careful with money. From Latin 'frux' (fruit, profit). 'A frugal household saves more.' Synonyms: thrifty, economical, prudent. Antonyms: extravagant, profligate, prodigal. Distractor 1 = extravagant / profligate. Distractor 3 = spendthrift. Distractor 4 = secretive.
questions.subject: Vocabulary

options.option_text: Stay silent and brooding in usual company
Talk excessively about often trivial things
Grow angry at every small remark or comment
Cry easily over small daily disappointments

questions.explanation: GARRULOUS — excessively talkative, especially on trivial things. 'The garrulous neighbour kept us up late.' Synonyms: loquacious, verbose, voluble. Antonym: TACITURN (reserved, silent). Distractor 1 = taciturn. Distractor 3 = irascible. Distractor 4 = lachrymose.
questions.subject: Vocabulary

questions.stem: A PRAGMATIC approach to a problem is:

options.option_text: Highly idealistic without practical concern
Practical and focused on workable results
Theoretical and lost in abstract argument
Emotional and based purely on instinct

questions.explanation: PRAGMATIC — practical, results-oriented. From Greek 'pragma' (deed, action). 'A pragmatic decision focuses on what actually works.' Synonyms: practical, sensible, realistic. Distractor 1 = idealistic. Distractor 3 = theoretical / abstract. Distractor 4 = impulsive / instinctive.
questions.subject: Vocabulary

questions.stem: A TACITURN companion tends to be:

options.option_text: Loud and talkative usually in any group
Reserved and saying little in conversation
Cheerful and energetic at all times
Aggressive and quick to argue with all

questions.explanation: TACITURN — habitually silent, uncommunicative. From Latin 'tacitus' (silent). 'The taciturn detective listened more than he spoke.' Synonyms: reticent, reserved, quiet. Antonyms: garrulous, loquacious, voluble. Distractor 1 = garrulous. Distractor 3 = jovial. Distractor 4 = belligerent.
